title: Credibility assessment of two implicit FEA models of a coronary stent under ASME V&V 40 across fatigue and radial strength mechanisms

models.name: M1: Stent-only implicit FEA
models.what_it_computes: Elastoplastic stress–strain response of the stent lattice through crimping, balloon expansion, recoil, and subsequent loading; local mean and alternating stress for fatigue safety factor; radial resistive force under uniform compression.

models.name: M2: Stent–artery implicit FEA
models.what_it_computes: Coupled contact mechanics of the stent with a hyperelastic anisotropic arterial wall and plaque analog; post-deployment residual field, contact pressures, stress amplification, and radial support with host-artery constraint effects.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism A: Deployment residual strains
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sets the mean stress and plastic strain from which fatigue cycles initiate and determines immediate post-deployment margin to yielding.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism B: Pulsatile fatigue
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Cyclic pressure and curvature drive alternating stresses that govern lifetime and risk of strut fracture.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism C: Acute radial strength
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Quasi-static uniform radial compression establishes support against vessel recoil and external crush.

clear_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported per model–mechanism on a 0–7 Credibility Index with mechanism-specific acceptance thresholds; matrices of scores are presented without mapping to standard ordinal levels.

sections: 1. Introduction
2. Device and computational problem statement

3. Context of Use (CoU): support nonclinical design verification by predicting (a) fatigue safety factor under ISO 25539-2 pulsatile loading with cyclic vessel curvature and (b) acute radial strength under quasi-static uniform compression; results are used to reduce, not replace, bench testing across labeled sizes

4. Model risk level and rationale: Medium—incorrect predictions could erode design margins, but decisions are corroborated by required physical tests and do not directly set patient treatment; model influence is moderate for each mechanism
5. Computational models
5.1 M1: Stent-only implicit FEA (geometry, material law, boundary conditions, and outputs)
5.2 M2: Stent–artery implicit FEA (artery constitutive model, contact, boundary conditions, and outputs)
6. Mechanisms of performance and failure
6.1 Mechanism A: Deployment residual strains
6.2 Mechanism B: Pulsatile fatigue
6.3 Mechanism C: Acute radial strength
7. Credibility plan and scoring approach (0–7 Credibility Index applied per factor and per model–mechanism, with predefined acceptance thresholds)
8. Software environment and quality assurance (toolchain description, version control, change management, and a brief note on implementation trustworthiness)
9. Discretization error assessment (systematic mesh refinement and local error indicators per model–mechanism)
10. Numerical solver error characterization (implicit convergence tolerances, contact stabilization, load stepping, and sensitivity to solver parameters)
11. Model inputs (material data, geometry tolerances, deployment parameters, and traceability to sources; input ranges and selection rules per mechanism)
12. Output comparison (benchmarks: crimp/deploy fixtures, pulsatile durability rigs, uniform radial compression; metrics, pass/fail bands, and replication)
13. Relevance of the validation activities to the CoU (representativeness of test articles, fixtures, and load spectra for each mechanism)
14. Results: credibility scores by model and mechanism (0–7 matrices)
14.1 Mechanism A: scores for M1 and M2 across all factors
14.2 Mechanism B: scores for M1 and M2 across all factors
14.3 Mechanism C: scores for M1 and M2 across all factors
15. Decision and residual risk within the CoU
16. Discussion
17. Conclusions
